items.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022
items.q: I remember calling up Wayne Shorter one time asking him for lessons. He said he didn’t give lessons but —

ctx.x: You mentioned that you mostly taught yourself and I read, and I believe this is from your web page. You said, “Many of the veterans of the period when you were learning were not inclined to mentor newcomers. Back then if somebody knew they weren’t going to tell you.” Is that an accurate reading?

I would say so. They’d say, “Oh man I don’t know what I’m doing, you know, just listen to records, learn tunes, listen to records, learn tunes.” I had the greatest saxophone teacher in the world, Joe Viola at Berklee that when I was in high school, tenth, eleventh, twelfth grade that’s who I studied with. And he would play piano and we’d play tunes. “Hey Joe what’s this, what is that, what is this flat nine here is that a — you know. So he was the greatest but he never said, you know, we just play together and…
So now you tell your students what to practice. People weren’t telling you but you tell them. Is that too simplistic?
